metadata.title: How to Play D&D 5.5e: Universal Edition
metadata.purpose: Complete shared player and Master Of Lore procedures, excluding canonical data stored in the other eight requested files.

system_identity.name: D&D 5.5e: Universal Edition — Covenant Engine
system_identity.core_promise: The world reacts honestly; gods, factions, and alignment create offers and consequences but never choose a player character's action.

basic_loop: MOL describes the situation, pressure, and obvious options.
If the result is certain or failure would add nothing, resolve without a roll.
Otherwise establish effect, risk, DC, Edge/Burden, and relevant proficiency.
Roll d20 plus ability modifier plus proficiency when trained.
Read the outcome band; the player may spend Resolve or Push when eligible.
Apply only a consequence that follows from the stated risk.
quickstart.test_formula: d20 + ability modifier + proficiency if trained + modifiers

outcome_bands.rule: total >= DC + 10, or natural 20 when possible
DC - 4 <= total < DC; player may accept stated cost
total <= DC - 10, or natural 1 when possible

blocks.text: The system keeps the parts of modern fifth-edition fantasy play that make characters readable and portable: six ability scores, d20 tests, proficiency bonus, Armor Class, hit points, Hit Dice, saving throws, spell ranks 1–9, concentration, resistance, vulnerability, class levels, subclasses, feats, and the level 1–20 proficiency curve.

It also keeps the existing Universal class contract. Every class has a hit die, primary abilities, two saving throw proficiencies, a canonical deity, a Bounty Ichor reserve, a core class engine, and three paths: melee/non-caster, half-caster, and full-caster. A class dossier wins if a specific feature conflicts with a general rule in this book.
The Covenant Engine adds or replaces the following shared procedures.

rows.Universal rule: Five outcome bands, declared stakes, and an optional Push
Three Beats plus one Reaction, with a compatibility translation for action and bonus-action features
Essential clues are found by competent approaches; rolls decide speed, clarity, safety, and extra leverage
Eight behavioral axes, Convictions, Ties, Resolve, Strain, Resonance, and Divine Claim
Composure, Stress, Fractures, and player-authored Scars
Era and Scale tags that change access and fiction without rewriting core math
AC prevents hits; Guard lets armor absorb a limited amount of harm
A Session Zero lethality mode and explicit Last Threshold choices
Hooks, redundant lore, multiple approaches, open resolutions, and honest consequence

blocks.text: This game borrows the purpose of useful mechanics, then implements that purpose in its own way.

rows.Purpose retained: Fast d20 familiarity, bounded numbers, class identity
rows.Covenant Engine implementation: Familiar statistics, PB curve, AC/HP, saves, spells, and levels

rows.Purpose retained: Flexible action use, degrees of outcome, clear modes of play
rows.Covenant Engine implementation: Three Beats, outcome bands, and Scene Modes

rows.Purpose retained: Clues, escalating risk, pushes, long-term psychological cost
rows.Covenant Engine implementation: Clue-forward tests, Pushes, Composure, Fractures, and Scars

rows.Purpose retained: Spotlight fairness, player currency, clocks, identity phrases
rows.Covenant Engine implementation: Spotlight checks, Resolve, clocks, Convictions, Ties, and Experiences

blocks.text: No rule requires dice when the result is certain or when failure would add nothing. Say yes, state the cost, or ask for a test only when the outcome can change the situation.
Apply rules in this order:

items: The group's Session Zero agreements and safety boundaries.
A specific class, ancestry, spell, item, creature, or scene rule.
This core rulebook.
A fifth-edition-compatible source converted using Chapter 20.
A fair table ruling that is recorded if it will recur.

blocks.text: A later canon package supersedes an older one on the same subject. For this edition, the Eight-Axis Covenant Alignment package supersedes older four-axis alignment text inside the life compendium. The newest twenty-two-class package governs classes. Current pantheon and race JSON governs names, creator categories, and deity relationships. Geographic coordinates and specific public-transport routes are not rules in this edition.
When an action is uncertain, risky, and consequential, make a test:
**d20 + ability modifier + proficiency, if trained + other modifiers**

The MOL names the ability and the target number. The player names the approach. If a skill, tool, vehicle, language, profession, or field of study clearly supports the approach, proficiency applies. Expertise adds proficiency a second time. Proficiency is never added more than twice.
The standard ability scores remain Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.

rows.Use: A trained person should usually succeed
A capable person has a fair chance
Training or a strong ability matters
A defining feat with rare leverage
Possible only through epic power, ideal conditions, or sacrifice

blocks.text: Do not increase a DC merely because a character is high level. Increase it when the task itself is harder. A locked household door does not become legendary because a level-17 hero touches it.
For attacks, a natural 20 is a critical hit and a natural 1 misses. For other tests, use the total and the fiction.

rows.Result: Total exceeds DC by 10+, or natural 20 when a breakthrough is possible
rows.Outcome: Breakthrough: success plus a strong benefit, speed, information, position, or reduced cost
Clean success: achieve the stated intent
Costly opening: the MOL offers success with a stated cost, reduced effect, delay, exposure, or hard choice; the player may accept or decline
Setback: the intent fails or succeeds only in a sharply limited way, and the situation changes

rows.Result: Total misses by 10+, or natural 1 when a crisis is possible
rows.Outcome: Crisis: a serious consequence follows from the established risk; it never invents an unrelated punishment

blocks.text: A natural 20 cannot accomplish something impossible, and a natural 1 does not make a competent character forget ordinary knowledge. Natural results change the band only when a breakthrough or crisis makes sense.
Before a consequential roll, establish four things in plain language:

items: Intent: what the character wants.
Approach: how they pursue it.
Effect: what success can accomplish.
Risk: what can happen if the attempt goes badly.

blocks.text: The MOL must reveal unavoidable or character-altering risks. Hidden facts can remain hidden, but the player should know the kind of danger being accepted.
Edge represents favorable circumstances. Burden represents unfavorable circumstances.

items: With one net Edge, roll 2d20 and keep the higher.
With two net Edge, roll 3d20 and keep the highest.
With one net Burden, roll 2d20 and keep the lower.
With two net Burden, roll 3d20 and keep the lowest.
Each Edge cancels one Burden. The maximum net rating is two.

blocks.text: Class features that grant advantage grant one Edge. Features that grant disadvantage grant one Burden. If a feature says a creature has advantage despite disadvantage, it sets the result to one Edge unless the feature says otherwise.

To Assist, describe a distinct contribution and possess relevant access, training, or leverage. The acting character gains one Edge. A helper shares any direct consequence that logically reaches the attempt.

For a group test, everyone rolls only when each person's performance matters. The group succeeds if at least half succeed; a Breakthrough counts as two successes and a Crisis subtracts one success. If one specialist can lead while others support, use one test with Assistance instead.
Resolve is a player's limited authority to reinforce what matters to their character. Each character can hold up to 3 Resolve.

Gain 1 Resolve when you willingly accept a meaningful complication or cost created by a Conviction, Duty, Tie, Temptation, or divine offer. The choice must change the scene; repeating harmless behavior does not generate Resolve.
Spend 1 Resolve to do one of the following:

items: Add 1d6 after seeing a d20 total but before the outcome is narrated.
Reduce incoming Stress by 2.
Refuse a Divine Claim complication that would otherwise require a cost, when the covenant rules allow resistance.
Declare a modest, plausible preparation tied to a proficiency, Experience, or earlier action.
Keep the spotlight long enough to complete one linked action when interruption would make the scene incoherent.

blocks.text: After a failed non-attack test, the player may Push once if they describe a new effort, sacrifice, tool, angle, or escalation. The MOL states a stronger consequence before the reroll. Roll again with one Edge and use the new result. A Push cannot be rerolled, and Resolve may modify it only if the declared consequence remains meaningful.
Pushes are never required to obtain an essential clue. They are for speed, completeness, leverage, rescue, concealment, or avoiding a consequence.

Each character writes two short Experience phrases at creation, such as “Raised in a Reef Court,” “Former Prison-Engine Inspector,” or “Never Abandon Chosen Family.” An Experience is broader than a skill but narrower than a personality.

Once per scene, when an Experience materially changes the approach, the player may either gain one Edge before the roll or add +2 after rolling. An Experience improves to +3 at level 9 and +4 at level 17. It never replaces a required tool, language, physical capability, or specific training.

items: Agree on campaign frame, era, starting level, lethality, and safety boundaries.
Choose a people, parent race, bloodline or lineage where applicable, and cultural upbringing.
Choose a background and two Experiences.
Assign ability scores.
Choose one of the twenty-two Universal classes and its path plan.
Record the class's canonical deity, Bounty Ichor trigger, Practices, and Hazards.
Choose Convictions, Ties, and initial alignment scores.
Choose proficiencies, languages, tools, equipment, and era permissions.
Calculate defenses, Guard, Composure, Stress Capacity, and resources.
Create three relationships: one trusted, one complicated, and one unfinished.

blocks.text: Ancestry never dictates morality, class, deity loyalty, culture, gender, or profession. Use four separate layers:

rows.Answers: What physical traits, senses, movement, resilience, or needs does the character have?
Which parent race, bloodline, lineage, transformation, or created origin shaped them?
Who raised them, what practices did they learn, and which community claims or welcomes them?
What name, gender, faith, identity, loyalties, and future do they choose?

blocks.text: Use the current `pantheon_and_races.json` for the canonical register. Mixed heritage is ordered and specific: combine inherited traits only within the campaign's ancestry budget, then choose culture independently. The MOL may reject a combination only for a clear balance or campaign-frame reason, not because the character crosses a social category.
Use one of these table-wide methods.

items: Standard array: 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8.
Point allocation: 27 points using familiar fifth-edition costs before ancestry/background adjustments.
Rolled: roll 4d6, drop the lowest, six times; any player may use another player's array so luck does not create a weaker participant.

blocks.text: Background grants +2 to one ability and +1 to another, or +1 to three different abilities, maximum 17 at level 1. Ancestry does not determine ability bonuses.
A background grants:

items: two skill proficiencies;
one tool, vehicle, language, or field proficiency;
one community contact;
one practical benefit that provides access rather than automatic success;
one of the character's two starting Experiences;
starting equipment appropriate to the campaign era.

blocks.text: Create backgrounds from lived roles rather than rigid careers. Examples include Archive Salvager, Ichor Clinic Attendant, Reef Advocate, Village Weatherkeeper, Faction Defector, Prison-Engine Worker, Court Interpreter, Monster-Sign Ranger, Sky-Ruin Archaeologist, or Orbital Habitat Technician.

The familiar skill list remains valid: Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Arcana, Athletics, Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, Religion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, and Survival.

Era-specific competence uses Field proficiencies rather than new ability scores. Common Fields include Alchemy, Computers, Engineering, Gunnery, Linguistics, Navigation, Piloting, Pressure Systems, Science, Starflight, Surgery, and Vehicle Repair. A Field pairs with whichever ability matches the approach.

rows.Formula: 8 + PB + higher of Wisdom or Charisma modifier, minimum 8
0 unarmored; 1 light; 2 medium; 3 heavy; +1 shield, maximum 4 unless a feature says otherwise
10 + Strength score; bulky items use 2–4 slots

blocks.text: Guard refreshes on a Field Rest if armor can be checked and repaired. Spend 1 Guard after damage is rolled to reduce that instance by PB + the armor's Guard value. Guard cannot reduce psychic damage, suffocation, poison already inside the body, or a source the armor could not plausibly intercept.

The default ten-year Universal campaign may begin at level 8, but this is a campaign start point, not a level cap or a universal rule. A level-8 character completes creation at level 1, applies seven level gains in order, selects the class path at level 3, and records all feats or ability improvements. Starting wealth and contacts should reflect an established professional, not a novice with inflated statistics.
The class dossiers were written using action, bonus action, movement, and reaction language. Translate them as follows.

rows.Covenant Engine cost: 1 Beat; only one feature with the Swift tag per turn

rows.Existing term: Action plus bonus action in one feature

blocks.text: Extra Attack remains part of one 2-Beat Strike; it never stacks with another Extra Attack feature. A feature that grants an additional full action grants 2 Beats, which expire at the end of the turn and cannot be used for another feature that grants extra Beats.
At level 3, choose one path in the class dossier.

items: Melee/non-caster paths use weapons, Thundercoils, positioning, and Bounty Ichor without spell slots.
Half-caster paths use spell ranks 1–5 and contribute half their class levels, rounded down, to multiclass slot progression after the path is chosen.
Full-caster paths use spell ranks 1–9 and contribute class levels minus 2, minimum 0, to multiclass slot progression because casting begins at level 3.

blocks.text: Path identity is protected. A general feat should not duplicate a path's signature engine more efficiently than the path itself.

To take a level in another class, have 13 in one of that class's listed primary abilities and explain how the training, awakening, bargain, adoption, or transformation occurs in the fiction. A character may have at most three classes unless the table explicitly chooses high-complexity play.

Use total character level for PB. Track class resources separately. Extra Attack does not stack. Spell slots use the contribution rules above; spells known or prepared remain class-specific. A multiclass character tracks a Duty for each class and the canonical covenant attached to each class. A bounty restores only the Bounty Ichor reserve of its own class unless a feature explicitly crosses that boundary.

items: A bounty trigger restores at most 1 Ichor per round and normally raises Resonance no more than once per session.
The same creature, object, or event cannot be recycled for Ichor, Resolve, alignment, or Resonance.
A class field is an ongoing effect; a character can maintain only one field with the same name.
A purely protective reaction reduced to 0 Ichor still expends the Reaction.
Thundercoil charges, heat, instability, and maintenance remain separate from Bounty Ichor.
Concentration remains one effect per creature unless a level-21+ Legacy Gift explicitly changes it.

blocks.text: Use the mode that matches the pressure. Changing mode does not erase the fiction.

rows.Procedure: Route choices, roles, Supply, hazard clocks
Projects, recovery, faction and settlement turns

blocks.text: In Free Play and Challenges, pass the spotlight when a character completes a meaningful action, a consequence demands a response, or another character is directly affected. Before giving a second consecutive spotlight to one player, check whether anyone else wants to act.

For large parties, place three spotlight tokens per player at the start of a complex scene. Spend one for each major action. A player with no tokens waits while an eligible player has tokens. Refresh all tokens when everyone has spent them or when the scene changes. Tokens track airtime, not action points.
Clocks make change visible.

rows.Use: Immediate obstacle, short ritual, simple chase
Standard investigation, dangerous journey, faction operation
Major project, settlement crisis, divine prison breach
Era shift, war, planetary threat, ten-year campaign transformation

blocks.text: Use a Progress clock for what characters are building or discovering and a Danger clock for what worsens. A Clean success usually fills 1 Progress; a Breakthrough fills 2. A Costly opening may fill 1 Progress and 1 Danger. A Setback usually fills 1 Danger. A Crisis fills 2 Danger or triggers the established consequence. Fiction can change these amounts.
Clocks do not predetermine an outcome. When a clock fills, resolve the event from current choices and conditions.

items: Establish objectives, positions, ranges, terrain, and any escape routes.
Determine awareness. An unaware creature has one Burden on initiative; it does not automatically lose its turn.
Roll initiative: d20 + Dexterity modifier, with relevant proficiency only if a feature grants it.
The highest result acts first. Then alternate between sides while possible. Each side chooses which eligible member uses its next slot. After every participant acts, begin a new round.

blocks.text: Alternating slots prevent one side from deciding the conflict before the other participates. A boss may have two or more initiative slots, but no single slot contains more than one turn.
On a turn, a creature has 3 Beats and one free object interaction. It has one Reaction from the end of its turn until the start of its next turn.

rows.Effect: Move up to Speed; movement may be split around actions
Make the attacks granted by the Attack action or use a standard offensive cantrip
Use the translated casting time: bonus action 1, action 2, longer special
Use one bonus-action feature; only one Swift feature per turn
Gain +2 AC until start of next turn or restore 1 spent Guard once per Field Rest
Movement this turn does not trigger opportunity attacks
Gain extra movement equal to Speed; at most twice per turn
Attempt to become Hidden when cover or concealment permits
Give one Edge to an ally's next eligible test before your next turn
Manipulate a complex object, administer an item, reload a demanding weapon, or perform a brief task
Name a trigger and a 1- or 2-Beat action; use the Reaction when it occurs
MOL sets cost by scope

blocks.text: You may repeat an action unless it has the Swift, Once, Reload, or Concentration limit. Strike includes Extra Attack, so repeating Strike is not allowed unless a feature explicitly grants an extra action or Beats.

Once per round, a player character may gain 1 extra Beat by marking 2 Stress. The extra Beat cannot cast a leveled spell, activate a Swift feature, or repeat Strike. A character at maximum Stress cannot Press.
Use a grid or range bands.

rows.Meaning: Large chamber, street, field, ship section
Requires sensors, special weapons, chase, or scene framing

blocks.text: A normal 30-foot Speed moves from Engaged to Near, or within Near, with one Step. Moving a full band at Far or beyond may require Dash, a vehicle, or a test. Exact printed ranges win when tactical precision matters.

Attack rolls target AC. A natural 20 hits and doubles all damage dice; flat modifiers are added once. A natural 1 misses. Exceeding AC by 10 is a Forceful Hit: choose one minor benefit appropriate to the attack—move the target 5 feet, deny its Reaction until its next turn, damage cover, or gain one Edge on the next action against it. A critical hit is also Forceful.
Half cover grants +2 AC and Dexterity saves. Strong cover grants +5. Total cover prevents direct targeting. Concealment normally imposes one Burden instead of changing AC.
Any creature can attempt these through a Strike or 1-Beat setup followed by a test.

items: Grapple: target chooses Strength or Dexterity save against 8 + PB + attacker's Strength modifier.
Shove: same save; push 5 feet or knock Prone.
Disarm: opposed attack test; on success, item lands within 5 feet. Creatures with a secure grip or integrated weapon gain one Edge.
Pin: while grappling, spend 1 Beat and win an Athletics contest; both are Restrained until the grapple ends, but the pinner may release freely.
Suppress: expend suitable ammunition or power to control a Near zone; crossing it requires a save or causes an opportunity attack.

blocks.text: A strong encounter has an objective besides reducing hit points: rescue, escape, hold, disable, expose, steal, seal, negotiate, survive, or choose between costs. Terrain should offer at least two meaningful interactions and one route that changes as a clock advances.

Minions have normal defenses and actions but 1 Hit. Any damaging hit defeats a minion; a failed save against damaging area effect also defeats it. Use minions for scale, not to disguise elite enemies.

Hit points represent stamina, luck, guard, pain tolerance, and the ability to avoid decisive injury. At half maximum HP or fewer, a creature is Bloodied. Bloodied has no universal penalty, but features and enemy behavior may reference it.
Damage, resistance, vulnerability, immunity, temporary HP, and healing otherwise use familiar fifth-edition rules.

Guard makes armor an active resource without replacing AC. Spend Guard after damage is rolled. If an attack exceeds AC by 10 or is a critical hit, it damages armor: after resolving the hit, the armor gains one Wear. At three Wear, its Guard maximum drops by 1 until repaired. At zero Guard maximum, armor still supplies AC but is compromised.
Improvised field repair clears one Wear with a DC 12 appropriate tool test and 10 minutes. A proper workshop clears all Wear during Downtime.

rows.Benefits: Spend one Hit Die or clear 1 Stress; once per Field Rest
Spend Hit Dice; restore Guard; recover short-rest features; clear PB Stress divided among party members through care or quiet

rows.Requirements: Secure shelter and at least 6 hours sleep or ancestry equivalent
rows.Benefits: Restore long-rest features and spell slots; regain half spent Hit Dice; heal to at least half HP, then spend Hit Dice; clear all ordinary Stress

rows.Requirements: Safety, treatment, food, and no adventuring
rows.Benefits: Heal Wounds, repair Scars when possible, treat Fractures, complete recovery projects

blocks.text: A Haven Rest does not automatically restore all HP. Comfortable medical care may restore additional Hit Dice or HP. This makes safe settlements, healers, supplies, and downtime matter without forcing an attrition-heavy style.

Composure protects against supernatural terror, divine intrusion, identity attack, psychic contamination, and overwhelming strain. When exposed, make an appropriate save against the source's Composure DC, or roll a Composure test: d20 + PB + higher of Wisdom or Charisma modifier.

rows.Stress: 0 and gain one useful insight or resistance
Choose 1 Stress or a brief reaction that changes position or access

blocks.text: Stress is not a diagnosis and never dictates a real-world disorder. At maximum Stress, the character is Overwhelmed: one Burden on concentration and Composure tests, and they cannot Press or voluntarily accept more Stress as a cost.
If a character would take Stress beyond capacity, they choose one:

items: become Incapacitated until the immediate danger passes or an ally reaches them;
take 1d8 psychic damage per overflow Stress and remain active;
take a Fracture and reset Stress to half capacity.

blocks.text: A Fracture is a temporary, player-authored response such as “Cannot trust mirrors after the dream court” or “Compulsively checks pressure seals.” It contains a Trigger, a Cost, and a Grounding method. The player portrays it. The MOL may invoke its Cost at most once per scene; accepting it grants 1 Resolve. Recuperation, support, magic, or a completed recovery project can heal or rewrite it.

A Scar is a lasting change chosen at the Last Threshold or after a campaign-defining trauma. It may be bodily, magical, relational, spiritual, reputational, or technological. A Scar grants an Experience-like +2 when its hard-won lesson applies and creates a real complication when its cost applies. It is not a punishment token.

sections.title: Zero hit points and the Last Threshold

blocks.text: At 0 HP, fall Prone and choose Fall or Stand.

items: Fall: become Unconscious and enter the Dying track.
Stand: remain conscious until the end of the current turn, gain one Wound, and take a final 2 Beats. Then fall Unconscious. A character can Stand only once per Haven Rest.

blocks.text: The Dying track has three boxes. At the start of a turn while dying, make a Constitution save, DC 10 plus current Wounds. Clean success marks no box; Breakthrough stabilizes; Costly opening marks one box but permits a final sentence or small interaction; Setback marks one; Crisis marks two. Damage at 0 marks one, or two for a critical hit. Healing removes the Dying track and restores HP normally.
When the third box would be marked, reach the Last Threshold and use the campaign's lethality mode.
Choose at Session Zero. A player may opt into a harsher mode for their own character but not a softer mode that changes the agreed campaign stakes without discussion.

rows.Last Threshold choices: Survive with a Scar; accept a divine/faction rescue with a stated Claim or debt; retire; or choose death
Make a final Constitution save. On success choose Scar, rescue debt, retirement, or death; on failure choose rescue debt, retirement, or death
Death occurs unless an already-established effect, immediate rescue, or resurrection applies; the player narrates the final moment

blocks.text: No mode authorizes surprise sexual violence, forced identity change, or another excluded subject.

sections.title: Resurrection and the Design of Death

blocks.text: Death in Universal is an administered passage, not a free reset. Resurrection requires a reachable soul, a body or true anchor when the effect requires one, consent of the deceased, and a valid method. The dead player always decides whether the soul returns.

Each return creates one Death Cost chosen collaboratively: a debt in Nefarokir's ledger, a lost or altered memory, a changed Tie, a visible death mark, a temporary reduction to maximum Hit Dice, a faction/legal complication, or a quest to repair the passage. A repeated return raises the cost or requires a rarer method; it never erases player authorship of the character.
Define destination, purpose, known routes, travel scale, and what makes the journey uncertain. Do not use a Journey scene when travel has no interesting decision.
Choose roles. One character may hold two roles in a small party but rolls only once per watch.

rows.Typical contribution: Vehicle, magic, pressure, medicine, weather, stars

blocks.text: Create a Progress clock and a Danger clock. Each watch, the party chooses pace: Cautious grants one Edge to hazard tests but uses 2 Supply; Steady uses 1 Supply; Urgent fills 1 Progress automatically but also fills 1 Danger and prevents a full Field Rest.

Supply is abstract. One Supply supports one character for one travel day or one party requirement such as a repair, environmental seal, medicine use, or special feed. A lack of Supply creates Exhaustion, Stress, equipment Wear, or lost time according to the fiction; it does not make food bookkeeping the only challenge.

Use tags rather than dozens of disconnected subsystems: Heat, Cold, Wet, Pressure, Vacuum, Toxic, Corrosive, Radiation, Low Gravity, High Gravity, Unstable Ground, Supernatural Weather, and Living Terrain. Protection provides a rating from 0–3. Exposure has an intensity from 1–4. If intensity exceeds protection, make an exposure save at each meaningful interval.
WorldBuilder determines which tags are present and how they change; the rules determine what characters do about them.

An essential clue is information needed to make a meaningful choice or reach another scene. A character with a plausible approach and access finds it without rolling. A test answers one or more of these questions:

items: How quickly is it found?
How complete or precise is it?
Is the search concealed?
What danger is avoided?
What extra leverage, contradiction, or weakness is uncovered?

blocks.text: Each important truth should exist in at least three forms: witness, record, physical trace, dream or omen, expert interpretation, enemy account, environmental change, or consequence. Destroying one source does not destroy the campaign.

Use an Evidence clock for complex cases. Breakthrough fills 2 and asks one free question. Clean success fills 1. Costly opening fills 1 with exposure, time, or a compromised source. A Setback still reveals the essential clue if the approach was competent, but fills Danger or gives the opposition time.
When a clue is earned, the player may ask a question supported by the approach:

items: What happened here?
What is being concealed or misrepresented?
Who or what had access?
What pattern connects these facts?
What will happen next if nobody intervenes?
What is vulnerable, missing, out of place, or newly changed?
Which account is least reliable, and why?

blocks.text: The MOL answers truthfully at the level earned. A partial answer may be incomplete; it cannot be deliberately false unless the clue itself is an identified lie.

NPCs have Needs, Fears, Boundaries, Leverage, and a starting Attitude: Hostile, Guarded, Open, Supportive, or Committed. A social roll cannot force an NPC to violate a hard Boundary, erase identity, create attraction, surrender bodily autonomy, or believe an obvious impossibility. It can change costs, timing, risk, interpretation, willingness to listen, or which option the NPC chooses.

For major negotiations, use paired 4- or 6-segment clocks: Accord and Fallout. Establish at least two possible agreements. Evidence, concessions, protection, public pressure, status, shared values, threats, and deception change effect and consequence. If Accord fills, the NPC accepts the negotiated terms they have heard. If Fallout fills, talks end, outside pressure intervenes, or the price changes.
Deception creates a hidden Truth clock. When consequences, witnesses, or contradictions fill it, the deception is exposed. The original roll determines plausibility, not permanent mind control.

Use a 6-segment Lead clock and a 6-segment Pursuit clock. Each round, participants choose a route and one chase action: Gain Ground, Create Obstacle, Bypass Hazard, Protect Passenger, Attack, Hide Trail, or Change Vehicle. Fill the relevant clock based on outcome bands. The quarry escapes when Lead fills; pursuers catch or force confrontation when Pursuit fills.
Offer at least two routes with different tags. A chase is about decisions and changing locations, not repeated identical speed rolls.
A Downtime turn is normally one week, adjusted to the fiction. Each character chooses two actions, or one intensive action.

items: Recover: heal a Wound, Fracture, Scar step, disease, or exhaustion.
Build or Repair: advance a crafting or infrastructure project.
Research: advance an Evidence or knowledge project.
Train: begin or advance a proficiency, language, feat, or class transition.
Connect: strengthen a Tie, contact, or community.
Serve: work for a faction, settlement, faith, or household.
Scheme: create leverage, cover identity, or hidden access.
Govern: change a policy, institution, resource, or public clock.

blocks.text: Roll only when uncertainty and consequence remain. Otherwise spend time and resources and advance the project.
Every project has Scope, Requirements, a Progress clock, a Danger or Cost clock when appropriate, and a Finish effect.

rows.Examples: Learn a language, repair rare armor, trace one lineage
Build a workshop, cure a local blight, expose an official
Establish a clinic, redesign defenses, reform a law
End a monopoly, build a fleet, change a divine prison function
Terraform, interplanetary network, end an Ichor economy

blocks.text: Money can meet Requirements and buy tools, but it does not replace expertise, consent, rare access, or time.
An item is defined by Chassis, Tier, Tags, Power Source, Load, and Quirks. A recipe is permission and understanding, not a compulsory shopping list.

To craft, meet the workshop and material Requirements, then fill Progress. On completion, choose one beneficial Quirk for a Breakthrough or accept a flaw if Danger filled first. Ichor and living technologies may develop Appetite or personality and must never be treated as inert merely because the crafter owns them.

At the end of a chapter or meaningful downtime, a settlement may take one turn. Record four ratings from 0–6: Safety, Provision, Cohesion, and Autonomy. Choose one Pressure and one Response. Advance a settlement project or danger clock. Then describe one visible change in ordinary life.

Player action can improve one rating while harming another. The settlement's people choose how they respond through established leaders, factions, customs, and conflicts; they are not passive reward containers.
Every mount, wagon, ship, submarine, skyship, aircraft, orbital craft, and starship uses the same statistics.

items: Scale 0–5.
Hull points and Hull Dice.
Defense and Armor.
Speed and Handling.
Systems: Drive, Control, Sensors, Life Support, Weapons, and Special.
Stations and Crew requirement.
Strain and Breaches.

rows.Example scope: Personal mount, bike, tiny skiff, exosuit
Train engine, patrol ship, bomber, corvette
Ocean liner, major skyship, frigate, habitat section

blocks.text: For each Scale of difference, the larger side gains one Edge on actions where mass, reach, armor, or output matters. At two or more Scale difference, personal weapons cannot damage Hull unless they have Breach, target an exposed system, enter the larger structure, or exploit a discovered weakness. Larger weapons may automatically destroy unprotected smaller objects, but named characters receive a save or consequence choice when the fiction permits.

rows.Common actions: Route power, repair, vent Strain, overdrive
Scan, target, jam, navigate, interpret environment
Cargo, medicine, passengers, boarding, special systems

blocks.text: A character at a station uses their own abilities and relevant Field. An unstaffed required station imposes one Burden or disables its actions.

Each vehicle turn has 3 Command Beats shared among staffed stations, plus one Reaction for the vehicle. Each station may act at most once per round unless a feature says otherwise. Personal turns may occur inside or around the vehicle at the same time.

Damage first reduces temporary Shields if present, then Hull. When a vehicle loses one quarter of maximum Hull in one hit or takes a critical hit, mark a Breach. Choose or roll an affected system. At three Breaches, it is Disabled; at five, it is Destroyed or catastrophically failing. Occupants get time to respond unless instant destruction was an agreed and clearly telegraphed risk.

Long voyages use Journey rules at the correct scale. A starship's “route” may be an orbital window, current, gate sequence, dream corridor, or interstellar transit solution. The rules do not require fixed setting coordinates. WorldBuilder can supply distances and environmental tags when that canon is ready.
Every extraordinary effect has a Source tag and one or more Effect tags.
Sources: Arcane, Divine, Primal, Psionic, Ichor, Biological, Chemical, Mechanical, Digital, Stellar, Planar, or Hybrid.
Effects: Attack, Control, Create, Detect, Heal, Move, Protect, Summon, Transform, Communicate, or Travel.

Source determines what can disrupt, detect, fuel, corrupt, or legally regulate the effect. Effect determines what it does. A technological invisibility field and illusion spell may both Conceal, but only the spell is automatically subject to antimagic and only the device is automatically subject to power loss or electronic warfare.
A counter must match a vulnerability.

items: Antimagic counters Arcane, Divine, Primal, and some Planar effects as stated.
Wards counter named Sources, creatures, or Effect tags.
Dispel removes an ongoing magical effect; it does not erase a mundane consequence the magic already caused.
Electronic warfare counters Digital sensors, control, or communication.
Engineering counters Mechanical systems.
Medicine, antitoxin, or bio-control counters Biological and Chemical effects.
Ichor grounding, dilution, sealing, or covenant action counters Ichor according to the item's state.

blocks.text: Hybrid effects require a counter to at least one essential Source. The MOL states what a successful counter can achieve before a player spends a scarce resource.

Use the class dossier's schools, casting ability, spell catalog, preparation, and progression. Rank is synonymous with spell level in this book. Concentration, components, range, duration, attacks, and saves remain in force.

When an old spell assumes a medieval object or environment, preserve its mechanical purpose and translate the expression. A spell that manipulates a door can affect an equivalent hatch; one that targets a beast does not automatically target a synthetic organism unless its tags say Beast or Biological and the conversion is fair.

A ritual is a Challenge with Requirements, a Progress clock, and a Danger clock. Participants take roles, spend components or access, and make meaningful choices. A ritual can reproduce a known ritual spell, extend scale or duration, combine sources, change a divine prison function, open long-distance passage, or accomplish a unique effect.
Large effects require large consequences, infrastructure, time, consent, rare leverage, or multiple completed projects. A single high roll does not bypass the agreed scope.
Thundercoils are optional equipment. They follow normal weapon proficiency and attack rules. Track Charge, Heat, Instability, Maintenance, and any Ichor Appetite separately from class Bounty Ichor.

items: A standard discharge spends 1 Charge.
An Overload improves one damage die step, range band, or area, then adds 1 Heat.
At Heat 3, further Overload adds 1 Instability and the weapon cannot clear Heat without a Field Rest and tools.
A Crisis on an Unstable Thundercoil creates a breach appropriate to its source and surroundings.

blocks.text: Class features can travel through a Thundercoil attack only when the dossier permits it. This never grants free Charge or Overload.

Use milestone advancement by default. The party advances when it has completed, transformed, abandoned with consequence, or decisively reframed enough major objectives to change its capabilities. Refusing the prepared quest does not block advancement; pursuing a player-created objective can qualify.

For XP play, use the familiar cumulative thresholds supplied in the current fifth-edition guide. Award XP for objectives, discoveries, rescues, negotiations, projects, hazards, and meaningful combat—not for killing alone. Everyone who participates in a chapter receives equal base XP.
At the end of a session, mark one Growth on a skill, Field, Experience, Tie, or project when it succeeded under meaningful stakes or a failure taught something costly. At three Growth, choose one:

items: rewrite the item to reflect what changed;
gain one Edge the next time it is central;
begin a downtime training project toward proficiency or Expertise;
improve an Experience at a tier boundary if the level rules allow.

blocks.text: Growth never raises ability scores or class level by itself.
At a class level granting an Ability Score Improvement, choose one:

items: +2 to one ability;
+1 to two abilities;
one full feat;
two minor talents approved by the MOL.

blocks.text: Ability scores normally cap at 20 before Legacy Ranks. A feat converted from another fifth-edition source must use the Beat translation and cannot create an infinite resource or repeated Strike loop.

After character level 20, advancement becomes ten Legacy Ranks rather than additional class levels. PB remains +6. Each rank grants one Legacy Gift from an allowed category; a category cannot be chosen at consecutive ranks unless the gift says repeatable.

rows.Gift: Ability cap +2 and one ability +2, or Epic feat
Mastery: Expertise in two skills/Fields or one new major proficiency
Covenant Gift tied to Resonance or a completed severance
Resilience: extra Wound capacity, Composure, or Guard option
Domain: establish or transform a group-scale institution, vessel, sanctum, or network
Apex improvement to one class engine, approved against its dossier
Scale Gift: act one Scale higher for one narrow purpose
Legendary ritual, invention, or relationship authority
Second Epic feat or Ability cap +2
Legacy Choice: apotheosis, mortality, office, voyage, transformation, retirement, or player-authored equivalent

blocks.text: Legacy Gifts expand scope more often than numbers. They should create new decisions rather than make ordinary party members irrelevant.
Agree on:

items: era and allowed technology;
starting level and advancement method;
Heroic, Perilous, or Brutal lethality;
horror intensity and Composure use;
lines, veils, pause tool, and check-in method;
divine coercion boundaries and character-specific forbidden transformations;
expected campaign length, party size, and scheduling;
whether alignment scores are public, private, or shared only during reviews;
rules for player-versus-player conflict, secrets, theft, persuasion, and romance;
how WorldBuilder and LifeSimulation information enters play.

blocks.text: Prepare situations, not required scenes.

items: State the Pressure: what is changing without the characters?
Give three Hooks connected to different player interests.
Place each essential truth in at least three sources.
Prepare at least four approaches: social, investigative, covert, ritual/technical, and direct where relevant; accept a sixth created by players.
Give every major faction a Need, Fear, Plan, Capacity, and Limit.
Create one Progress and one Danger clock.
List several possible resolutions and their honest costs; leave room for an unforeseen one.
Ask which unresolved player Tie or Conviction can be invited, not compelled.

blocks.text: Use the lightest consequence that follows from the established risk.

items: Reveal trouble or a hard choice.
Spend time, Supply, position, secrecy, or opportunity.
Add Stress, Wear, Instability, or faction Heat.
Advance a Danger clock or separate allies.
Inflict damage, a condition, a Wound, or loss of access.
Change a relationship, institution, region, or divine state.

blocks.text: Never use a consequence merely to restore the planned plot.

For a quick first pass, set a budget in Threat Points (TP). Each player character contributes 4 TP for a Standard conflict, 3 for a Light conflict, 5 for a Hard conflict, or 6 for an Extreme conflict.
Rate enemies relative to party level.

rows.Enemy: Elite, two levels higher or with two strong turns
Boss, three+ levels higher or multi-phase

blocks.text: Add 1–4 TP for severe terrain, an advancing ritual, protected civilians, or another objective that consumes actions. Subtract 1–4 for strong allied support or a decisive prepared advantage. This is a playtest calibration tool: creature accuracy, control, area damage, and action count matter more than the printed label.

A boss should have multiple decision points, not inflated HP alone. Use two initiative slots, telegraphed reactions, breakable defenses, phase changes, environmental control, and a non-damage objective. Never give a boss unlimited interrupts. Each reaction names a trigger and cost.

Secret notes can create delight, but essential campaign understanding cannot depend on one player remembering to reveal one note. Distinguish player knowledge from character knowledge without forcing players to perform ignorance in ways that make play worse. If dramatic irony is fun, use it openly.

Describe sensory and supernatural pressure, then return authorship of internal response to the player. The MOL may offer impulses or reactions; the player chooses how the character experiences them unless a short condition explicitly applies. Avoid real-diagnosis stereotypes. A Fracture is a game-state consequence and story prompt, not a claim about mental illness.

WorldBuilder owns terrain, maps, planetary geometry, environment tags, era state, locations, and physical world simulation. LifeSimulation owns NPC identity, schedules, reactions, conversations, relationships, and social consequences. The Covenant Engine owns tests, resources, clocks, conflict, harm, advancement, alignment, covenant state, and campaign consequence.
No system silently overwrites another system's authority.

rows.Required fields: id, level, classes, abilities, proficiencies, HP, Guard, Stress, alignment, covenants, ties
id, location, schedule state, needs, fears, boundaries, attitude, faction, relationship, current reaction
mode, participants, environment tags, era, scale, progress clocks, danger clocks
semantic id, biome tags, hazard tags, settlement rating, controlling factions
standing, trust, heat, influence, plan clocks, known information
scale, hull, systems, stations, strain, breaches, power source
hooks, lore sources, resolutions, clocks, status, consequences

blocks.text: The engine may emit events such as `test_resolved`, `clock_changed`, `relationship_changed`, `alignment_reviewed`, `resonance_changed`, `claim_changed`, `npc_reaction_requested`, `settlement_turn_completed`, `era_changed`, and `vehicle_breached`.

WorldBuilder and LifeSimulation may propose tags and consequences, but the MOL confirms mechanical changes. Dialogue generation cannot spend player resources, move alignment, accept a divine bargain, or speak for a player character.

LifeSimulation should derive an NPC reaction from knowledge, relationship, schedule, current need, faction pressure, and witnessed action. It must not read inner alignment as public fact unless the NPC has a credible magical or institutional method. Reactions can change Personal Trust or faction Heat; the MOL confirms the final rating.
Use familiar fifth-edition conditions with these clarifications and additions.

rows.Effect: Cannot see; attacks have one Burden; attacks against you have one Edge; sight-dependent actions fail
Cannot attack or directly harm the source; source has one Edge on social tests; does not control decisions or create attraction
Cannot hear; hearing-dependent actions fail
Rating 1–6; subtract rating from d20 tests and reduce Speed by 5 feet per two ratings; death at 6
One Burden on tests while source is perceptible; cannot willingly move closer unless you spend 1 Beat bracing
Speed 0; ends when grappler is unable to hold or target escapes
Unseen and location uncertain; ends through exposure, detection, or obvious action
Cannot spend Beats or Reactions; concentration ends
Cannot be seen without a special sense; does not automatically hide sound, tracks, heat, scent, or disturbance
Cannot Press; one Burden on concentration and Composure tests
Incapacitated; Speed 0; Strength and Dexterity saves fail; close hits are critical
Transformed into inert substance; Incapacitated, resistance to damage, immune poison/disease, does not age
One Burden on attacks and ability tests
Crawling costs double; standing costs 1 Beat; close attacks gain Edge, distant attacks gain Burden
Speed 0; attacks have Burden; attacks against gain Edge; Dexterity saves have Burden
Incapacitated, Speed 0, Strength and Dexterity saves have Burden; repeat save at end of turn when effect permits
Incapacitated, unaware, Prone, drops held items; close hits are critical

items: Which clocks changed, and why?
Which faction or settlement learned what?
Did a Conviction, Tie, Duty, or Temptation create a meaningful cost and Resolve?
Did behavior justify alignment movement?
Did an edict, anathema, bargain, or bounty change Resonance or Claim?
Did everyone receive meaningful spotlight?
What consequence is now visible, and which hook is optional next?

rows.Conversion: Field Rest; features recover once the 10-minute rest completes
Haven Rest; features recover, but HP follows this book's rest rule
Use Composure, Stress, Fracture, and Scar
Translate to one or more axis thresholds and demonstrated conduct
Add Scale, Systems, Stations, Strain, and Breaches

blocks.text: If a feature was balanced around one action and one bonus action, it normally costs all 3 Beats. If a feature grants an action, grant 2 temporary Beats. If it grants movement, grant a free Step with the stated restrictions. A feature cannot create more than one extra Strike per turn unless it explicitly represents a level-17+ apex and has a limited use.

Keep AC, HP, ability scores, saves, attacks, damage, resistances, and spell DCs. Translate actions by cost. Give a standard creature 3 Beats; its Multiattack is a 2-Beat Strike. Give a legendary creature extra initiative slots or telegraphed Reactions instead of unrestricted legendary actions. Convert lair actions to a visible environment clock or a fixed end-of-round event.
The following rules require table data and should be reviewed every three sessions:

items: whether three Beats allow too much movement or too many defensive stacks;
Guard reduction at each tier;
Stress Capacity and the cost of Press;
encounter Threat Points for parties larger than six;
vehicle Scale interactions and Hull damage;
Legacy Gifts above level 20;
Haven Rest healing pace;
frequency of Resolve, Resonance, and alignment movement.

blocks.text: Change one variable at a time. Record the old rule, new rule, reason, start date, and affected characters. Do not retroactively punish choices made under an earlier version.

This is an unofficial homebrew rules system for the Universal setting. It is not an official Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, Call of Cthulhu, or Daggerheart product. Names used in the design genealogy identify the traditions examined in the user-supplied research files. The Covenant Engine's procedures are original implementations written for Universal. Existing third-party or official content remains subject to its own license and is not reproduced here.

Rules exist to make choices clear, costs meaningful, characters distinct, and consequences trustworthy. When a rule would erase a reasonable choice without adding safety, clarity, or dramatic weight, pause and repair the rule. Universal can be dangerous, hungry, divine, and vast without becoming a machine that plays the characters for their players.

authorityRules: Generated NPC dialogue cannot spend player resources or speak for a player character.
NPC reactions use witnessed or credibly learned conduct, not hidden alignment.
WorldBuilder tags propose conditions; the MOL confirms mechanical consequences.
Era changes track Discovery, Infrastructure, Access, and Social Adoption separately.
No coordinate or public-transport route data is embedded in this bridge.

thundercoils.overload: Improve one damage die step, range band, or area; add 1 Heat.
thundercoils.heat_3: Further Overload adds 1 Instability; Heat requires a Field Rest and tools to clear.
thundercoils.unstable_crisis: Creates a breach appropriate to the source and surroundings.
thundercoils.separation: Charge, Heat, Instability, Maintenance, and Ichor Appetite are separate from class Bounty Ichor.
